result: Shamsi accepted all four with changes, against four rejections in round 4. Every build used cards that link on the two doorway pages, the secondary navigation with a compact filter bar, the views as a second row, and placeholders for the figures; no build used the light header. Every automated check passed. What is left is hierarchy: status lines, explanations, category lists and filters still push the main content down, and no build reviewed its layout for that. Two builds used the public logo on an internal tool, and one used a page zone on these dense pages.

A.notes: No page CSS. Uses page zones on two pages, against the rule that dense pages do not.

B.notes: Six rules on tokens (placeholder, IDs in mono, a link row). The public logo on an internal tool.

C.notes: Thirteen rules on tokens, including its own stack spacing utilities; one class used with no rule. The public logo on an internal tool.

D.notes: Six rules on tokens (placeholder, status row, category list). Admin logo, standard header.

patterns: All four: .ds-card--link on both doorway pages, .ds-subnav with a compact filter bar, .ds-subnav--in-page for the views, placeholders, the standard header. None used the light header.
Three of four wrote their own placeholder style; each looked different.
None reviewed the page for what is primary; descriptions, status lines and category lists sit above the main content in all four.
Sort for the activity charts was a filter-style select with Apply in all four; the live site uses buttons that sort at once.
Predictions: 1 right (all four used cards that link). 2 right (all four put the filters in the navigation bar). 3 wrong (no build used the light header).
findings: Agents do not review their layout for what is primary: explanations, status lines and filters still push the main content down. The docs say the main content comes first, but nothing tells an agent to check before finishing.
Two builds used the public logo on an internal tool; the docs do not say plainly that internal tools use the internal logo.
Missing patterns: a placeholder for content still to come, and a sort control that applies at once.
next: Add a review pass for agents and the internal logo rule, settle the placeholder and sort patterns, then run the reports once more.
